title: Bloch eigenfunction expansion and band derivatives
notes: Each \(f_t\) is expanded in \(y_{t,n}\), with coefficients written without a complex conjugate; the notes then mention computing \(d\lambda/dt\).
statement: Choose an orthonormal eigenbasis \(\phi_{n,\theta}\) of each fiber. Then \(Uf(\theta,\cdot)=\sum_n\langle Uf,\phi_{n,\theta}\rangle\phi_{n,\theta}\) in \(L^2(0,T)\), with the complex conjugate in the inner product. If \(\lambda_n(\theta)\) is simple, gauge to periodic \(v=e^{-i\theta x/T}\phi\); then \(\lambda^{\prime}_n(\theta)=\langle v,[-2iT^{-1}(D+i\theta/T)]v\rangle\) for normalized \(v\).
reconstruction: The derivative formula is a labeled reconstruction by differentiating the gauged operator; no such formula survives in the notes.
fate: \citet[\S1, pp.~54--58 of the Russian original]{novikov1974periodic} recalls this classical Floquet theory; the paper was received on 18 February 1974 and published later in 1974.

title: Monodromy in a conjugate solution basis
notes: With \(\lambda=k^2\), initial data \((y,y_x)=(1,ik)\), the pair \(y,\bar y\) gives \(T=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\\bar b&\bar a\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), \(|a|^2-|b|^2=1\).
statement: For real \(k\ne0\) and real \(u\), those two solutions are independent because their Wronskian is nonzero. Transfer by one period has determinant one and the conjugation symmetry stated in the notes. Its half trace \(d(\lambda)=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}T=\operatorname{Re}a\) is independent of the basepoint and extends as an entire function of \(\lambda\).
reconstruction: The basis restriction \(k\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\) is essential; for other spectral parameters one uses a real initial-data fundamental matrix, not the claimed conjugate basis.

title: Floquet multipliers and spectral bands
notes: The multipliers are \(a_R\pm\sqrt{a_R^2-1}\); bounded solutions are equated to \(|a_R|\le1\), and outside the strip the notes write \(e^{\pm t}\).
statement: For real \(\lambda\), the multipliers solve \(\rho^2-2d(\lambda)\rho+1=0\), and \(\sigma(L)=\{\lambda:|d(\lambda)|\le1\}\). Inside an open band all solutions are bounded. At a band edge at least one nonzero bounded periodic or antiperiodic solution exists, but the second solution can grow linearly. In a gap the real multipliers are \(\pm e^{\pm\kappa}\), with a common minus sign when \(d<-1\).
reconstruction: The edge quantifier and the omitted negative-multiplier case are restored.
fate: \citet[\S1, pp.~54--58 of the Russian original]{novikov1974periodic} recalls this classical Floquet theory; the paper was received on 18 February 1974 and published later in 1974.

title: Monotonicity of the discriminant in each band
notes: Novikov says monotonicity was proved for small potentials; Gelfand announces a \ru{конкурс на доказательство} for the next meeting.
statement: For any real smooth periodic potential, is \(d_{\lambda}(\lambda)\ne0\) whenever \(|d(\lambda)|<1\)? Equivalently, does each noncollapsed band interior map monotonically onto \((-1,1)\)? The answer is yes; critical values of the real Hill discriminant lie outside the open strip.

title: Constant potentials and the free monodromy
notes: For constant \(u\), Gelfand says the spectrum is positive. The later free matrix has diagonal entries \(e^{\pm iT}\) and \(a_R=\cos T\), omitting spectral dependence.
statement: For \(u\equiv c\in\mathbb R\), \(\sigma(-D^2+c)=[c,\infty)\) and \(d(\lambda)=\cos(T\sqrt{\lambda-c})\), analytically continued below \(c\). For \(c=0\), the plane-wave basis at \(\lambda=k^2>0\) gives \(\operatorname{diag}(e^{ikT},e^{-ikT})\). All finite gaps are closed.

title: Mathieu stability sketch
notes: The equation is \(-y^{\prime\prime}+(a+b\cos2x)y=0\); the first stability band is associated with \(a+b\cos2x<0\), followed by a contrast with constant coefficients.
statement: For each real \((a,b)\), stability of the Mathieu equation is governed by the trace of its period-\(\pi\) monodromy: at least one bounded solution exists precisely when its half trace has absolute value at most one. The inequality in the notes does not specify whether it is pointwise, averaged, or a statement along a parameter curve, and does not identify an exact first-band boundary.
reconstruction: Only the well-defined monodromy criterion is supplied as context; the sketch is not promoted to a new theorem.
fate: Floquet stability is classical; \citet[\S1]{novikov1974periodic} supports the trace criterion. No exact publication match is claimed for the ambiguous inequality or sketch.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The general criterion is established, but the intended parameter-region assertion remains unidentified.

title: Closed gaps and double boundary eigenvalues
notes: Periodic and antiperiodic points have \(|a_R|=1\); a double degeneracy has \(b(x_0,\lambda_n)\equiv0\).
statement: For real periodic scalar \(L\), a closed finite gap is a double eigenvalue of the relevant periodic or antiperiodic problem. Its monodromy is \(M=\pm I\); in any admissible conjugate basis \(b=0\). At an open-gap edge the boundary eigenvalue is simple and \(M\) is a nontrivial Jordan matrix with eigenvalue \(\pm1\).
reconstruction: The claim \(b\ne0\) is restricted to nonzero real \(k\) where the notebook basis exists; the basis-independent formulation uses \(M\).
fate: \citet[\S1, pp.~54--58 of the Russian original]{novikov1974periodic} recalls this classical Floquet theory; the paper was received on 18 February 1974 and published later in 1974.

title: Which supplementary data determine a periodic potential?
notes: The half trace does not determine \(u\). The notes ask which scattering data beyond the spectrum do, mentioning Dubrovin and Faddeev's students.
statement: At a fixed basepoint, supplement the band spectrum of a real smooth finite-gap Schrödinger operator with its Dirichlet divisor: one point on each real gap oval of the hyperelliptic spectral curve, including its sheet, with the usual endpoint identification. These data determine the potential. Band edges alone leave an isospectral family and cannot even distinguish translations.
reconstruction: The finite-gap restriction and sheet-labelled divisor are added explicitly; no unrestricted theorem is inferred solely from the finite-gap reference.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--3]{novikov1974periodic} develops the stationary spectral curve. \citet[Chapter~2, \S3, pp.~84--87 of the Russian original, especially Eqs.~(2.3.11)--(2.3.12)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} gives one sheet-labelled pole on each gap oval, its evolution, and the trace formula reconstructing the potential. These pages were read. The latter paper was received 2 June 1975 and published in 1976. This is an exact answer in the finite-gap scope, a partial match to the notes' unrestricted periodic wording.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The finite-gap inverse problem is established. General periodic inverse spectral theory also requires supplementary data; the finite-gap reference here is not represented as proving the general theorem.

title: Finite-gap periodic potentials
notes: Eventually all boundary eigenvalues become double and the forbidden intervals shrink to points.
statement: A real smooth periodic potential is finite-gap if only finitely many bounded complementary intervals of \(\sigma(-D^2+u)\) are nonempty. Equivalently, all sufficiently high periodic/antiperiodic pairs coincide. The half-line below the bottom of the spectrum is not counted as a finite gap.
fate: \citet[\S2]{novikov1974periodic} uses this precise spectral class.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established in the stated scope; no unresolved claim is inferred from this occurrence.

title: Stationary KdV and finite-gap spectra
notes: If \([A,L]=P(u,\ldots)\) is multiplication and \(P=0\) has a periodic solution, the potential is finite-gap; the converse is also asserted. The next page specifies one operator at every odd order and their linear combinations.
statement: For real smooth periodic \(u\), a nontrivial odd-order differential operator \(A\) commuting with \(L=-D^2+u\), with nonzero constant leading coefficient, forces finitely many open gaps. Conversely a smooth real periodic finite-gap potential satisfies a stationary equation of the KdV hierarchy. A trivial commuting operator \(A=p(L)\) is not a sufficient hypothesis.
reconstruction: The indispensable odd-order/nontrivial condition is obtained from the following page, not from the isolated theorem sentence. The converse is separated from the forward theorem.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2.1 and its stationary construction, pp.~59--62]{novikov1974periodic} is the near-contemporary primary publication. The finite-gap inverse and converse framework is developed in \citet{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The converse is explicitly proved in Chapter~2, \S3, statement3, p.~86 of the Russian original of \citet{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}, which was also read.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established in the stated scope; no unresolved claim is inferred from this occurrence.

title: Finite-dimensional Hamiltonian stationary flows
notes: The stationary hierarchy equations are Hamiltonian systems with \(n\) degrees of freedom and a maximal set of commuting integrals.
statement: Fix a nondegenerate stationary KdV equation of order \(2n+1\) and integrate its translation-invariant first integral once. On the resulting regular \(2n\)-dimensional phase space, the induced finite-dimensional flow has a Hamiltonian structure and \(n\) independent commuting integrals on a regular open set. Singular levels and loss of independence are not covered by the Liouville-torus conclusion.
reconstruction: The regular-level and independence qualifications distinguish Liouville integrability from a claim about every singular point.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2.1, pp.~59--61]{novikov1974periodic} supplies the stationary Hamiltonian systems and commuting integrals; manuscript received 18 February 1974.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established in the stated scope; no unresolved claim is inferred from this occurrence.

title: Density of finite-gap potentials
notes: Novikov asks \ru{любой ли потенциал аппроксим. конечнозонными?}; neither function space nor topology is stated.
statement: For every real \(q\in H^m(\mathbb R/T\mathbb Z)\), \(m\ge0\), and every \(\varepsilon>0\), does a real periodic finite-gap \(q_*\) exist with \(\|q-q_*\|_{H^m}<\varepsilon\)? Yes. In particular smooth periodic potentials can be approximated in any prescribed finite collection of Sobolev seminorms.
reconstruction: The periodic setting comes from the talk; the real Sobolev topology and quantifiers are an explicit modern formulation, not written in the notebook.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.2 and its proof in \S5]{grebertkappelerposchel2004gaps} proves finite-gap density in \(H^m\), \(m\ge0\), attributes the question to Novikov, and credits the first proof to Marchenko--Ostrovskii's 1975 characterization of Hill spectra. The author-hosted full PDF was downloaded and these passages read. The manuscript was received 15 September 2003, revised in 2004, and published in 2004. First-proof credit is distinguished from the later proof actually inspected.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Affirmatively settled in every real Sobolev space \(H^m\), \(m\ge0\); it is not a C/D candidate.

title: A stationary matrix equation and its spectral polynomial
notes: A traceless \(2\times2\) matrix \(\Lambda\) satisfies \(\Lambda^{\prime}=[\Lambda,Q]\). Its eigenvalues are written \(\pm\sqrt{\det\Lambda}\), followed by the words the word polynomial.
statement: For any differentiable traceless matrix solution \(\Lambda_x=[\Lambda,Q]\), its characteristic polynomial is \(\mu^2+\det\Lambda\); hence \(\mu=\pm\sqrt{-\det\Lambda}\) and \(\det\Lambda\) is independent of \(x\). In the stationary KdV construction a suitable gauge and spectral parameter yield polynomial coefficients of the spectral curve. The square roots themselves are generally algebraic functions, not polynomials.
reconstruction: The notes mix \(\delta\), \(\delta^2\), and a \(\delta^{-1}\) gauge term; no exact matrix-degree assertion is recovered without fixing that gauge. The polynomial claim is safely assigned to the determinant/spectral polynomial.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~61--62]{novikov1974periodic} constructs the matrix and spectral polynomial. The sign follows independently from the characteristic polynomial of a traceless \(2\times2\) matrix.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established in the stated scope; no unresolved claim is inferred from this occurrence.

title: Riccati expansion and conservation-law densities
notes: \(\psi_k=e^{ikx+\int_{-\infty}^x\chi}\), \(\chi=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_nk^{-n}\), and \(I_n=\int_{\mathbb R}\chi_n\) are conserved.
statement: For a nonvanishing local solution of \(-\psi_{xx}+u\psi=k^2\psi\), put \(\psi^{\prime}/\psi=ik+\chi\). statement: For the periodic oscillator just specified, \(\sqrt{\omega^2-k^2}\int_{u_-}^{u_+}\sqrt{E-V(s)}\,ds\) is proportional to its action. General two-variable modulation imposes a conservation law for an action density and flux, not an unspecified constant throughout space-time. A constant action can arise only after a further reduction or normalization that is not recorded.
reconstruction: The proportionality to oscillator action is identified; the missing reduction is not invented.
fate: \citet[abstract and nonlinear-wave variational formulation]{whitham1970twotiming} describes two-timing and averaging. The article was received 10 January 1970 and published in 1970, before the 1974 exposition; the Caltech primary repository metadata and abstract were opened. The primary article is a thematic match for action averaging; no exact reduction producing the notebook's particular constant relation has been verified.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The intended constant-action reduction remains unidentified; the standard formal modulation method is established.

title: The smooth wavefront set
notes: \((x_0,\xi_0)\notin WF(u)\) if a localization \(\varphi(x_0)\ne0\) has Fourier transform decaying faster than every power in a cone around \(\xi_0\).
statement: For \(u\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)\), \(\xi_0\ne0\), choose \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)\) with \(\varphi(x_0)\ne0\) and an open conic neighborhood \(V\) of \(\xi_0\). The point is outside \(WF(u)\) when for every \(N\ge0\) a constant \(C_N\) satisfies \(|\widehat{\varphi u}(\xi)|\le C_N(1+|\xi|)^{-N}\) for all \(\xi\in V\). The same localization and cone serve for all \(N\).
fate: \citet[Proposition~2.5.5 and its concluding equivalence, pp.~122--123]{hormander1971fourier} is exact. The paper appeared in 1971 and developed material circulated in the 1969 Nordic summer-school lectures.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established in the stated scope; no unresolved claim is inferred from this occurrence.

title: Step functions, boundary normals, and smoothing
notes: A step across a line and the characteristic function of a disk are drawn, with normal directions; convolution with a delta-like sequence is suggested.
statement: If \(\Omega_0\) has a smooth boundary and \(u=1_{\Omega_0}\), then locally at each smooth boundary point \(WF(u)=N^*(\partial\Omega_0)\setminus0\). A smooth nonvanishing jump across a hypersurface has the same conormal set. Mollification approximates the distribution; conic rapid decay is uniform only away from the indicated wavefront directions, with the relevant microlocal convergence conditions.
reconstruction: Smoothness of the boundary and a nonzero jump are supplied; corners would add other directions.
fate: \citet[\S2.4 and pp.~125--126]{hormander1971fourier} develops conormal distributions and smoothing in the wavefront pseudotopology. This is explanatory classical content, not a new singularity theorem by Tulovskii.

title: Gelfand's slicing explanation of directional singularities
notes: Gelfand reduces a planar Fourier integral to a one-dimensional oscillatory integral in a sliced function \(\psi(t)\); drawings contrast tangent and transverse cuts of a circle.
statement: For a smooth compactly supported density on a domain with smooth boundary, integrating over level sets of a linear coordinate produces a smooth density near transverse intersections. At critical values where the level hyperplane is tangent to the boundary, this pushforward can be singular. Such critical directions are conormal directions; stationary-phase decay depends on the local geometry and degeneracy.
reconstruction: The original \(\varphi\) in the planar integral cannot be a globally smooth compactly supported function if a boundary jump is intended. The characteristic-domain factor and the transversality qualification are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S1.2 and Proposition~2.5.7]{hormander1971fourier} gives the oscillatory framework. The precise scalar slice density is an explanatory reconstruction of the drawings, not an exact formula recoverable from them.

title: Wavefront projection equals singular support
notes: \(\pi WF(u)=\operatorname{sing\,supp}u\), \(\pi(x,\xi)=x\).
statement: For every distribution on a smooth manifold, the projection of its smooth wavefront set to the base manifold is its singular support. In particular \(WF(u)=\varnothing\) if and only if \(u\) is smooth.
fate: \citet[\S2.5, definition and Fourier characterization]{hormander1971fourier} establishes this fundamental property.

title: Schwartz kernels and the required continuity
notes: Every \(P:C_c^\infty(\Omega)\to C^\infty(\Omega_1)\) is assigned \(K_P\in\mathcal D'(\Omega\times\Omega_1)\).
statement: If \(P:C_c^\infty(X)\to\mathcal D'(Y)\) is continuous in the standard test-function and distribution topologies, there is a unique distribution kernel \(K\in\mathcal D'(Y\times X)\) satisfying \(\langle Pu,v\rangle=\langle K,v\otimes u\rangle\). Mere linearity without continuity is insufficient.
reconstruction: Continuity is supplied, and output-first kernel order is fixed for all subsequent modern formulas.
fate: \citet[\S2.5, discussion preceding Theorem~2.5.12, p.~129]{hormander1971fourier} applies the classical kernel theorem in this setting.

title: Extension to compactly supported distributions
notes: If the kernel wavefront contains no point with either component covector zero, \(P\) extends from test functions to \(\mathcal E'(\Omega)\to\mathcal D'(\Omega_1)\).
statement: For \(K\in\mathcal D'(Y\times X)\), assume \((y,0;x,\xi)\notin WF(K)\) for every nonzero \(\xi\). Then the kernel pairs with arbitrary compactly supported distributions in \(X\), defining \(P:\mathcal E'(X)\to\mathcal D'(Y)\). Excluding also \((y,\eta;x,0)\), \(\eta\ne0\), removes source-independent output singularities. No global support condition is needed for a compactly supported input and compactly supported output test function.
reconstruction: The two zero-component exclusions have different roles; their joint sufficient condition in the notes is retained.
fate: \citet[p.~130, discussion preceding Theorem~2.5.14]{hormander1971fourier} gives the kernel action on compactly supported distributions and precisely the zero-output-covector obstruction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established in the stated scope; no unresolved claim is inferred from this occurrence.

title: The primed canonical relation and its sign
notes: The notebook orders the kernel coordinates as input \(x\), output \(y\), but reverses the output covector \(\eta\) in its definition of \(WF'(P)\).
statement: With output-first kernel \(K(y,x)\), define \[C_P=\{(y,\eta;x,\xi):(y,\eta;x,-\xi)\in WF(K)\}.\] Using input-first ordering, the same relation is written \[\{(x,\xi;y,\eta):(x,-\xi;y,\eta)\in WF(K)\}.\] Thus it is the input covector that must change sign when the relation acts on \(WF(u)\) without another sign reversal.
reconstruction: Both coordinate order and the sign convention are written explicitly; this is more than simply reversing the order of factors in a composition formula.
fate: \citet[Eq.~(2.5.9) and Theorem~2.5.14, p.~130]{hormander1971fourier} fixes the input sign in the operator relation. A simultaneous sign reversal can conceal the discrepancy for real kernels, but not for arbitrary complex kernels.

title: Wavefront propagation through a kernel
notes: \(WF(Pu)\subset WF'(P)\circ WF(u)\) under the zero-component exclusions.
statement: Under both exclusions of the preceding extension item, for compactly supported \(u\), \(WF(Pu)\subset C_P\circ WF(u)\), where \(C_P\) uses the corrected input-sign convention. Without the exclusion of kernel points with input covector zero, an additional output-wavefront term is necessary.
reconstruction: The notebook's stronger two-sided exclusion permits its short formula once the canonical-relation sign is repaired.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2.5.14, pp.~130--131]{hormander1971fourier} proves the estimate under the stated zero-component exclusions. The preceding Theorem~2.5.12 gives the extra output term for smooth inputs when that exclusion is absent.

title: Composition of kernel relations
notes: For \(Q\circ P\), the notes write \(WF'(P)\circ WF'(Q)\) and explicitly define composition in input-first order.
statement: Suppose \(P:X\to Y\) and \(Q:Y\to Z\) have kernels with the zero-component exclusions and enough proper support in the intermediate variable for the composition to be defined. Then, in output-first convention, \(C_{QP}\subset C_Q\circ C_P\). The notebook's reversed written order is consistent with its explicitly defined input-first convention and is not itself an error.

title: Distribution spaces with controlled wavefront
notes: For a closed conic \(\Gamma\subset T^*\Omega\setminus0\), the notes write \(\mathcal D_\Gamma=\{u\in\mathcal D':WF(u)\subset\Gamma\}\), without a prime on the left.
statement: Write \(\mathcal D'_\Gamma(\Omega)=\{u\in\mathcal D'(\Omega):WF(u)\subset\Gamma\}\). Hörmander's original convergence means weak distribution convergence together with rapid Fourier decay estimates converging to zero on every compactly localized closed cone disjoint from \(\Gamma\).

title: Multiplication under the no-opposite-covectors condition
notes: If \(\Gamma_1+\Gamma_2\) avoids zero covectors, multiplication extends uniquely and continuously into the cone union \(\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2\cup(\Gamma_1+\Gamma_2)\).
statement: For closed conic sets with \(\Gamma_1\cap(-\Gamma_2)=\varnothing\), the product \(uv\) is canonically defined for \(u\in\mathcal D'_{\Gamma_1}\), \(v\in\mathcal D'_{\Gamma_2}\), and \(WF(uv)\subset\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2\cup(\Gamma_1+\Gamma_2)\). The extension agrees with smooth multiplication and is sequentially continuous for the original Hörmander convergence, which gives uniqueness by smoothing. 'Continuous' is not an unrestricted assertion of joint continuity for an unspecified locally convex topology.

fate: \citet[Theorem~2.5.10, pp.~126--127]{hormander1971fourier} is an exact 1971 match. \citet[Introduction and multiplication theorem]{brouderdanghelein2016continuity}, first circulated on arXiv in September 2014 and published in 2016, distinguishes sequential continuity from topological continuity and proves hypocontinuity in the normal topology.

title: Homogeneous phases and symbol classes
notes: A phase is real, homogeneous of degree one in \(\Theta\), with total differential nonzero. Symbols obey \(|\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\Theta^\beta a|\le C_{\alpha\beta}(1+|\Theta|)^{m-\rho|\beta|+\delta|\alpha|}\).
statement: Let \(\varphi\) be smooth on a conic subset of \(X\times(\mathbb R^N\setminus0)\), real, positively homogeneous of degree one, with \(d_{x,\Theta}\varphi\ne0\). For a sufficient standard class take \(0\le\delta<\rho\le1\); a smooth amplitude is in \(S^m_{\rho,\delta}\) when the displayed estimates hold uniformly on each compact \(x\)-set for all multiindices. Nondegeneracy of the critical manifold is an additional assumption needed for the usual nondegenerate FIO calculus; it is not part of the recorded phase definition.
reconstruction: Smoothness, compact-set quantifiers, an admissible parameter range, and the distinction between a phase and a nondegenerate phase are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S1.1, \S1.2, and phase definition]{hormander1971fourier} is the direct source.

title: Cutoff definition of an oscillatory distribution
notes: \(\langle A,u\rangle=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\int e^{i\varphi}a\chi(\varepsilon\Theta)u\,dx\,d\Theta\), with compactly supported \(\chi=1\) near zero.
statement: With a phase and symbol as above, local compact support in \(x\) after pairing with a test function, and the amplitude cut off near \(\Theta=0\) where necessary, integration by parts defines an oscillatory distribution. For \(\rho>0\) and \(\delta<1\) in the standard symbol setup, the cutoff limit exists distributionally and is independent of \(\chi\). To define an operator, use a kernel phase in both output and input variables; the formula displayed on the page itself defines a distribution.

title: The one-soliton wave and its normalization
notes: The equation is \(4f_t+f_{xxx}+ff_x=0\), followed by \(f=2\lambda^2\operatorname{sech}^2[\lambda(x-\lambda^2t-h)]\).
statement: For \(\kappa>0\) and \(h\in\mathbb R\), \(q(t,x)=2\kappa^2\operatorname{sech}^2[\kappa(x-\kappa^2t-h)]\) solves \(4q_t+q_{xxx}+6qq_x=0\), has amplitude \(2\kappa^2\), and speed \(\kappa^2\). It does not solve the notebook's coefficient-one equation except in the zero solution limit.

fate: \citet[\S1, Eq.~(1.8)]{lax1968integrals} gives the classical solitary wave in another amplitude/time normalization. The Russian translation and its derivation were read. Direct substitution here independently identifies the missing factor 6.

title: Two-soliton asymptotic separation
notes: A two-soliton solution is written schematically as two pulses plus \(O(e^{-\varkappa t})\) as \(t\to+\infty\).
statement: For the reflectionless KdV two-soliton solution with distinct \(\kappa_1,\kappa_2>0\) and positive norming constants, the field separates as \(t\to\pm\infty\) into two solitary waves with speeds \(\kappa_j^2\), amplitudes \(2\kappa_j^2\), and asymptotic centers \(h_j^\pm\), with an exponentially small remainder for this finite pure-soliton family. This does not assert exponential decay of radiation for arbitrary decaying initial data.
reconstruction: The finite reflectionless class, distinct positive parameters, and both time limits are explicit reconstruction; the notebook displays only the positive limit.
fate: \citet[\S2]{lax1968integrals} studies two solitary waves before the seminar. The inverse-scattering setting also appears in \citet{shabat1973kdv}; that paper's general radiative asymptotics are not the exponential estimate claimed for this reflectionless special case.

title: Uniqueness of a prescribed pure two-soliton solution
notes: The notes assert uniqueness: \ru{можно док., что оно единственно}.
statement: Within the regular real reflectionless class, the two distinct discrete eigenvalues and their positive norming constants uniquely determine the potential and its KdV evolution. Equivalently, specifying the complete outgoing two-soliton scattering data determines this member of the pure-soliton family. Merely specifying two speeds, without positions/norming constants or excluding radiation, is insufficient.

title: The damaged collision-amplitude bound
notes: Problem 1 asks for total amplitude at collision and writes \(|f(t,x)|\le2\sum_{j=0}^{n}\lambda_j(\lambda_{j+1}-\lambda_j)\), \(\lambda_0=0\), with an uncertain upper summation limit.
statement: The general task is to bound a pure multi-soliton profile during interaction in terms of its discrete spectral parameters. The displayed proposed bound cannot be made a definite theorem from the surviving ink: the upper index is uncertain, parameter ordering is absent, and the indicated upper limit requires an undefined \(\lambda_{n+1}\).

title: Collision-induced shifts of soliton centers
notes: Problem 2: the centers shift; calculate the displacement. The answer is described as standard scattering.
statement: For a regular real two-soliton solution with \(\kappa_1>\kappa_2>0\), compare the intercepts of the incoming and outgoing center trajectories. They satisfy \(\Delta h_1=\kappa_1^{-1}\log[(\kappa_1+\kappa_2)/(\kappa_1-\kappa_2)]\) and \(\Delta h_2=-\kappa_2^{-1}\log[(\kappa_1+\kappa_2)/(\kappa_1-\kappa_2)]\). Thus the larger soliton advances and the smaller one is delayed. In the regular finite \(N\)-soliton family, shifts add pairwise.
reconstruction: The notebook gives no formula. The reflectionless hypothesis, positive ordered wave parameters, and the definition outgoing minus incoming are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S2]{lax1968integrals} is the pre-seminar two-wave source. The precise normalized pairwise formula is independently visible in \citet[Eqs.~(2.4)--(2.5)]{bonnemaindoyonel2022hydrodynamics}; that modern restatement is not claimed as first publication.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The classical inverse-scattering phase shifts answer the recorded question.

title: Bargmann potentials and polynomial-exponential solutions
notes: A Bargmann potential is characterized by two solutions of \(y_{xx}+(q+\zeta^2)y=0\) of the form \(P_{1,2}(x,\zeta)e^{\mp i\zeta x}\), polynomial in \(\zeta\).
statement: For a regular real decaying finite reflectionless potential, suitable spectral normalizations of the Jost solutions give polynomial-exponential functions of \(\zeta\); they are independent at generic spectral parameters. They cease to be independent at the discrete spectral points, and real regularity is a separate restriction on the data. The notebook's algebraic property may also describe complex or singular potentials if those restrictions are omitted.
reconstruction: Generic spectral independence, permissible spectral rescaling, and the distinction between formal algebraic and regular real scattering potentials are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S3, especially the Schrödinger specialization]{shabat2014interpolation} identifies this construction and references Shabat's 1970 work on zero-reflection potentials. The general classical reflectionless line is already present at 1970-219.3. The 1970 original was not opened and is not treated as a verified exact interpolation source.

title: Rational interpolation for the auxiliary solutions
notes: \(P/Q=c_j e^{2i\zeta_jx}\) at the interpolation nodes and \(P/Q=1\) at infinity. The number of nodes is written \(2n\,?\,1\), with an overwritten sign. The notes claim arbitrary parameters produce a fundamental system of a scalar Sturm--Liouville equation.
statement: A precise related theorem uses \(P,Q\) of degrees \(m,n\), \(N=m+n\), and \(N+1\) distinct interpolation nodes \(k_j\), with \(P(k_j)/Q(k_j)=c_j e^{-2k_jx}\). On an interval where the interpolation system is nondegenerate, normalize the leading coefficients by \(p_0q_0=1\). Then \(e^{kx}P\) and \(e^{-kx}Q\) solve a common equation \(\psi_{xx}=(k^2+ku_1+u_2)\psi\). Obtaining an ordinary Schrödinger potential with \(u_1=0\), and a globally regular real potential, requires additional reduction and positivity/reality conditions.
reconstruction: This is a separately labeled modern reconstruction from the 2014 theorem, with \(k=i\zeta\) up to swapping the two solutions; it is not a decipherment of the obscured node-count sign.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1, \S3, pp.~313--315 of the Russian original]{shabat2014interpolation} is a close mathematical match and explicitly mentions the 1974 Gelfand seminar on p.~305. It appeared forty years later, not 'soon after'. The source's unrestricted scalar assertion is therefore classified F: the missing reduction prevents an exact theorem identification, despite unusually strong provenance.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The nondegenerate rational-interpolation construction is published; the notebook omits restrictions needed for its stronger scalar and arbitrary-parameter wording.

title: Polynomial Wronskian and the missing normalization
notes: \(P_xQ-Q_xP-2i\zeta PQ=\prod(\zeta-\zeta_j)\). The preceding line has \(y_1=Pe^{+i\zeta x}\), \(y_2=Qe^{-i\zeta x}\).
statement: If the ratio condition has exponent \(+2i\zeta_jx\), the polynomial \(W_0=P_xQ-Q_xP-2i\zeta PQ\) vanishes at each node. Under the matching degree and leading-coefficient hypotheses, \(W_0=-2i\,p_0q_0\prod_j(\zeta-\zeta_j)\). It is the Wronskian \(y_1'y_2-y_1y_2'\) for \(y_1=Pe^{-i\zeta x}\), \(y_2=Qe^{+i\zeta x}\), with these corrected exponents. In the 2014 normalization the analogous constant is \(-2\).
reconstruction: The degree restriction and leading factor are restored. No independence is asserted at zeros of this Wronskian.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1 and its proof]{shabat2014interpolation} proves the polynomial identity with its leading coefficient. The vanishing follows directly by differentiating the interpolation data; the notebook omitted the normalization and reversed the compatible exponential assignment.

title: Cubic time evolution of reflectionless data
notes: \(c_j(t)=c_j(0)e^{2i\zeta^3t}\), substituted into the same interpolation relation.
statement: At each fixed node, take \(c_j(t)=c_j(0)e^{2i\zeta_j^3t}\). In a compatible regular reflectionless reduction, the cubic time factor is the KdV scattering evolution after the notebook's time rescaling. For \(\zeta_j=i\kappa_j\) the combined factor is \(e^{-2\kappa_jx+2\kappa_j^3t}\), giving center speed \(\kappa_j^2\). Arbitrary unconstrained complex interpolation parameters need not give a globally nonsingular real solution.

fate: \citet[\S3]{shabat2014interpolation} revisits interpolation and soliton dynamics, while \citet{shabat1973kdv} gives the earlier inverse-scattering evolution. This is the known cubic-flow mechanism, not a proof of the notebook's unrestricted construction.

title: The incomplete auxiliary time operator
notes: \((4\partial_t+\partial_x^3-3q\partial_x)P=(\qquad)Q=0\); the second operator is left empty.

Conjugating a differential time operator on full eigenfunctions by \(e^{\pm i\zeta x}\) generally introduces \(\zeta\)-dependent terms; these cannot simply be suppressed when the same letter denotes only the polynomial factor.

title: Riccati logarithmic derivatives and the Miura map
notes: \(f=\partial_x\log(Pe^{?i\zeta x})\), \(4f_t+f_{xxx}+3(f^2+\zeta^2)f_x=0\), and \(f_x+f^2=q\) are said to give \(4q_t+q_{xxx}+6qq_x=0\).
statement: For the recorded Schrödinger equation, any nonvanishing local solution has logarithmic derivative \(v=y_x/y\) satisfying \(v_x+v^2=-q-\zeta^2\). Independently, a consistent Miura normalization is: if \(v_t-6v^2v_x+v_{xxx}=0\), then \(u=v_x+v^2\) satisfies \(u_t-6uu_x+u_{xxx}=0\). Indeed its residual equals \((\partial_x+2v)(v_t-6v^2v_x+v_{xxx})\). Time rescaling and a constant spectral shift give equivalent conventions, but do not make all displayed notebook signs and coefficients mutually consistent.

fate: \citet{miura1968transformation} is the 1968 historical source; its primary PDF could not be opened, so the bibliographic entry is explicitly unverified. The algebraic identity is proved directly by expansion and checked independently in the supplied code. \citet[\S1]{lax1968integrals} supplies the earlier Riccati/conservation-law context.

title: Representations of diffeomorphism and current groups
notes: Kirillov announces descriptions of representations of \(G_1=\operatorname{Diff}M\) and \(G_2=H^M=C^\infty(M,H)\), with \(H\) a group.
statement: For a smooth manifold \(M\) and a finite-dimensional Lie group \(H\), the smooth current group is \(C^\infty(M,H)\) with pointwise multiplication. A representation-classification problem requires a topology, representation category, regularity, and equivalence notion. None is specified on the page, and no classification assertion can be recovered.

fate: \citet[\S2]{araki1970factorizable} is a verified earlier source for continuous tensor-product and current-group representations, but its measurable-current framework is not an exact match for an absent Kirillov theorem. Related earlier material occurs at 1970-228.5 and 1972-291.6--291.9.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The announced representation description is unspecified; it does not define a new open classification problem.

title: The bundle-automorphism group extension
notes: For a principal bundle \(E\to M\) with structure group \(H\), its automorphism group projects onto \(G_1\) with fiber \(G_2\).
statement: For a smooth principal \(H\)-bundle \(E\to M\), the exact group sequence is \(1\to\operatorname{Gau}(E)\to\operatorname{Aut}_H(E)\to\operatorname{Diff}(M)_{[E]}\to1\). The image consists of diffeomorphisms whose pullback bundle is isomorphic to \(E\). The gauge group is the smooth sections of \(E\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}H\), not generally \(C^\infty(M,H)\). For a chosen trivialization of a trivial bundle, all diffeomorphisms lift and the extension is a semidirect product with the ordinary current group.
reconstruction: The subgroup preserving the bundle isomorphism class and the adjoint-bundle gauge group replace the unrestricted base and fiber. The Lie-group topology theorem is not imported into the 1974 claim.
fate: \citet[introduction and bundle-automorphism extension theorem]{wockel2007symmetry} states the precise modern extension, with its additional Lie-group hypotheses. The elementary group-level distinction is a correction of the notebook's omitted trivial-bundle assumption, not an attribution of Wockel's 2007 theorem to Kirillov.

title: Unit-speed propagation of singularities and caustics
